newsitem.title: RWANDA: WFP says 700,000 Zaire refugees unaccounted for.
newsitem.headline: WFP says 700,000 Zaire refugees unaccounted for.

text.p: The head of the United Nations food aid organisation said on Wednesday there were still 700,000 Rwandan refugees unaccounted for in Zaire,

Catherine Bertini, Executive Director of the World Food Programme, told a news conference that two years of supplying nutrition to Hutu refugee camps led them to believe that last week's mass exodus of Hutus to Rwanda "was not the full story".
"We have been feeding in the camps for a long time and providing food for 1.2 million refugees," she said. "These figures have been consistent for two years and we have no reason to doubt them."

Bertini said the fate of those remaining in eastern Zaire -- where a rebel rout of government troops sparked last week's march of 500,000 Rwandan Hutus back to their homeland -- meant the need for an intervention force was still urgent.
"There are 700,000 still unaccounted for. Their safety and ability to eat is still a need," she said.

Major-General Paul Kagame, vice-president and defence minister of Rwanda, told a news conference earlier on Wednesday that he believed the numbers of refugees in camps in Zaire had ben exaggerated and the bulk of them had returned.
The Hutu refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 in the wake of a massacre of up to a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus blamed chiefly on the former Rwandan army and Interahamwe militia.

The half-million Hutu refugees left the north of eastern Zaire after a Zairean rebel force -- made up of ethnic Tutsis and believed by some to be supported by Rwanda --laid seige to camps in order to flush out the killers hiding in their midst.
Bertini said the WPF had reports that over 100,000 refugees from south-eastern Zaire were now trekking north towards Goma, scene of last week's exodus.

In Ottawa Canadian Defence Minister Doug Young, whose troops would lead the multinational intervention force now increasingly in doubt, said hundreds of thousands appeared to be heading from the south of eastern Zaire to the Rwandan border.

"Information we have seems to indicate strongly enough that hundreds of thousands more that might still be in the region are on their way from the southern part of the eastern region of Zaire towards Bukavu to return to Rwanda," he said.
But Bertini said she was very concerned for those remaining and "the substantial number" who had fled further west into Zaire.
"Our responsiblity is to reach and feed those people in need," she said. "In order to do that we need a force."
A United Nations-led meeting is been held in Germany on Friday to discuss how an intervention force can help provide aid to refugees in zaire.
But there are clear signs that international will for a force is waning and Kagame said on Wednesday it was unneccesary.

Bertini said the need for a force remained, adding that there was a clear need for weapons to be removed from any former Rwandan soldiers or Interahamwe if the intervention force's missions was to succeed.
"What soldier would want to protect refugees if there were people with arms with them," she said.
